Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
1245 PM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Through Friday: Hot and mostly dry (very slight chance of an
  isolated sea breeze shower/storm). Heat indices near advisory
  criteria. 

- Scattered showers and thunderstorms possible by the weekend.
 
- Next week's outlook features seasonably hot conditions w/ a
  chance of isolated afternoon showers/storms.  

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1210 AM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

The mid/upper pattern remains amplified, with the Lone Star State
under the influence of a strong ridge over western and central
CONUS. Ridging should remain strong, perhaps strengthen somewhat
through Friday. Ensemble guidance continues to suggest a modest
increase in mid/upper pressure heights through Friday. This will
keep conditions hot and mostly dry, with a slight chance of an
isolated sea breeze related shower or thunderstorm. Leaning a tad
cooler than the NBM worked well for us yesterday. So I went with a
mix of NBM and 25th percentile NBM for our Thursday / Friday
highs. But don't be fooled by the word "cooler." Highs are still
expected to reach the upper 90s to around 100 in most inland
areas. Dew points are expected to mix down into the low 70s today,
then upper 60s to low 70s on Friday (higher at the coast). Heat 
indices likely to be near advisory criteria, with most areas 
peaking between 105F and 108F.

The pattern remains amplified going into the weekend. However,
the ridge should retrograde into west CONUS while downstream 
troughing (currently over E CONUS) pushes westward. Ensembles are 
in good agreement with this scenario, showing a 500MB height drop
from ~595dm on Friday to ~587dm by Sunday. Guidance is rather 
aggressive with an amplifying, positively tilted, deep trough on 
Sunday that extends from the Great Lakes into the southern 
Mississippi River Valley. An associated surface low is expected to
push eastward across the Midwest over the weekend, with its 
trailing cold front pushing into E TX by Saturday. The front 
should be weak and increasingly diffused as it approaches our 
region. But it may supply sufficient lift in a less capped 
environment to allow for scattered shower and thunderstorm 
activity Saturday afternoon through early Sunday. This activity 
could be limited to our northern zones on Saturday, before pushing
farther south Saturday night into early Sunday. 

Long range guidance suggests that ridging returns next week. For
now, we are leaning towards seasonably hot and humid conditions
with a chance of isolated sea breeze related showers / storms. 

Self 

&&

.AVIATION...
(18Z TAF Issuance)
Issued at 1244 PM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

The MVFR ceilings observed in the northern TAF sites this morning 
have lifted and given way to VFR conditions, which will mostly 
prevail for this period. Isolated SHRA are possible with the 
afternoon sea-breeze, but model confidence is too low to mention in 
the TAFs. MVFR cigs/vis are possible overnight and early Friday 
morning in the northern TAF sites within the 1000 to 2000 ft 
layer, which will burn off by mid morning.

JMG

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1140 PM CDT Wed Jul 29 2026

Light to moderate southwesterly winds and 2-3 foot Gulf seas are
expected through Friday. By Saturday, an approaching frontal
boundary is expected to tighten the low-level gradient, increasing
southwesterly flow to 15-20 knots, possibly higher, by Saturday
afternoon and night. Seas may increase to 4 feet as a response to
the increasing winds. Caution Flags will likely be warranted.
Scattered showers and thunderstorms associated with the front are
possible Saturday night into Sunday. The outlook for early next
week features light to moderate southwesterly winds, 2-3 foot
seas, and a slight chance of isolated showers/storms along the sea
breeze boundary. 

&&

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
1214 PM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dangerous heat continues through Saturday with afternoon highs in 
the mid 90s to near 100 and heat indices of 105-110F.

- The Heat Advisory has been expanded to include all of southeast 
Texas and southwest, Central and south central Louisiana this 
afternoon.

- A few showers may develop this afternoon. Better precipitation
  chances return Sunday with afternoon pop up thunderstorms
  expected each day next week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(Today through Wednesday)
Issued at 1228 AM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

Persistence is the forecast philosophy in the short 
term as a strong upper level ridge remains in place across much of 
the southwest and south central conus. Despite this, a sliver of 
higher moisture extending from the southeast Louisiana coast up 
through the Dakotas will offer a low end chance (20%) for a couple 
of afternoon showers or thunderstorms across south central Louisiana 
this afternoon. For the rest of us, the heat remains on with 
afternoon highs climbing into the mid to upper 90s with afternoon 
heat indices in the 105-112 range. The Heat Advisory has been 
expanded west with this package to now include all of southeast 
Texas and southwest Louisiana. 

Little movement to the upper ridging will keep conditions largely 
uniform through Saturday. The ridge finally retreats west Saturday 
night into Sunday as an upper level trough and a rare weak surface 
frontal boundary digs through the central U.S. Guidance is very 
split on whether the frontal boundary will reach the coast and even 
if it does, the effect on sensible weather this far south will be 
minimal with perhaps a few degrees drop in dewpoints. The boundary 
will, however, increase PoPs Saturday night into Sunday bringing the 
first appreciable rains to most of the region in over a week. As the 
boundary stalls out and dissipates, a weak gradient aloft will allow 
for diurnally driven afternoon convection to develop each day next 
week. The added cloud cover and precip will keep afternoon highs 
closer to climatological normals in the lower 90s with max heat 
indices from 100-105.

Jones

&&

.AVIATION...
(18Z TAFS)
Issued at 1212 PM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

The CU field developing along the sea breeze will cause brief
periods of MVFR ceilings this afternoon along the I-10 corridor. A
brief shower may also occur, but mainly at LFT or ARA. Generally
southwest winds are anticipated during the period.

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1228 AM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

Light winds and low seas are anticipated through Saturday. 
A weak boundary will drift to near the northern gulf coast Saturday 
night into Sunday which will increase winds to 15-20 knots over the 
coastal waters. The boundary will also increase thunderstorm 
chances. Light southerly flow becomes reestablished Monday through 
the rest of the week.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1228 AM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

Hot and humid conditions will continue through the 
end of next week. Rain chances will increase Saturday night into 
Sunday as an upper level trough and weak frontal boundary approach 
the area. A brief period of northwesterly winds could develop 
Sunday, but will quickly turn back out of the south Sunday night 
into Monday. Scattered afternoon thunderstorms will develop each day 
next week.
